_meta.title: Indigenous-Specific Grant Opportunities — Seattle / Pacific Northwest
_meta.purpose: A living reference of funders that specifically prioritize Tribal nations and Native-led/Native-serving organizations in and around Seattle and the wider Pacific Northwest. Built to feed the AI Grant Writer's funding-source lookup and to support applications (e.g. to a regional 'PNW Impact' style award) that ask applicants to show they've identified real, relevant local funding partners.
_meta.howToMaintain: Each entry has a lastVerified date and a sourceNotes field describing where the info came from. Funder priorities, award ranges, and whether applications are even open change often (see e.g. ANA's SEDS program, replaced in FY2026) — re-verify any entry whose lastVerified date is more than ~2 months old directly against its url before relying on it in a submission, and update lastVerified when you do. Add new entries at the bottom of the grants array following the same schema; do not delete an outdated entry, set its applicationStatus to reflect what changed instead so the history of what was tried is preserved.
_meta.verificationCaveat: Every entry below was checked against public sources as of lastUpdated, but funder guidelines, deadlines, and award amounts are exactly the kind of factual details this project's backend refuses to let the AI invent — confirm current details on the funder's own page before citing them in a real application.

grants.name: Potlatch Fund
grants.eligibilitySummary: Tribal governments, Native 7871 organizations, Native-led 501(c)(3) nonprofits, and Native-led community groups with fiscal sponsorship, serving residents of WA, OR, ID, or MT. Individual Native artists (in-region) may apply to the Native Arts program directly.
grants.typicalAward: Community Building grant up to $5,000/year; Native Arts grant up to $5,000/year; InterTribal Canoe Journey support up to $1,500/year; additional unrestricted support periodically available through the Community Relations & Innovation Fund
grants.applicationStatus: Open — annual cycles per program; check site for current cycle dates
grants.deadlineNotes: Varies by program; each runs roughly once a year
grants.pnwImpactFit: Seattle-headquartered, Native-led, and explicitly regional (WA/OR/ID/MT) — a natural funding partner or reference point for any application arguing PNW-specific Indigenous community impact.
grants.sourceNotes: potlatchfund.org, capaa.wa.gov funding page, Instrumentl grant listing, Artist Trust resource page (all cross-checked 2026-09-12)

grants.name: Na'ah Illahee Fund
grants.based: Seattle, WA (programming based at Daybreak Star Indian Cultural Center, Discovery Park)
grants.geographicScope: Primarily Seattle/Puget Sound; some programs extend to AK, BC, OR, ID, MT, WA region-wide
grants.type: Indigenous women-led regional grantmaking + capacity-building fund
grants.eligibilitySummary: Varies by program. The Indigenous Arts & Culture (ARTS) grant (City of Seattle-funded) is open to Indigenous applicants only, for events/activities within the City of Seattle. The Food Sovereignty and Yahowt Land & Food Restoration programs support Indigenous-led community food/land projects across the wider region.
grants.typicalAward: Varies by program cycle; not a fixed published amount across all programs
grants.applicationStatus: Open on a rolling/cyclical basis — check current funding opportunities page
grants.howToApply: Apply via naahillahee.org/community-funding/ (Submittable-based application per program)
grants.deadlineNotes: Program-specific; check community-funding page for the active cycle
grants.pnwImpactFit: Seattle-based and Seattle-specific for its City of Seattle-funded ARTS grant — a strong, directly local match for any Seattle-focused Indigenous impact narrative.
grants.sourceNotes: naahillahee.org (Community Funding and Indigenous Arts & Culture Grant pages), Anthropocene Alliance profile, Seattle Urban Native Nonprofits directory (cross-checked 2026-09-12)

grants.name: Seventh Generation Fund for Indigenous Peoples — Community Vitality grants
grants.funder: Seventh Generation Fund for Indigenous Peoples
grants.based: Eureka, CA (HQ) — national reach, PNW tribes and Native orgs eligible
grants.eligibilitySummary: Native Peoples' organizations/projects; must be Indigenous/Native-led (at minimum 80% of board/leadership); one grant per calendar year per applicant; must be in good reporting standing on any prior grant.
grants.applicationStatus: Open — check site for current cycle; historically rolling/periodic
grants.deadlineNotes: No fixed annual deadline publicized as of last check — monitor 7genfund.org/make-a-difference/apply-for-a-grant/
grants.pnwImpactFit: Not PNW-specific, but a credible national Native-led funder to pair with regional funders — useful for demonstrating a diversified, Indigenous-led funding base in a competitive application.
grants.sourceNotes: 7genfund.org, 7genfund.submittable.com application page, hinchilla.com funder profile, GrantStation (cross-checked 2026-09-12)

grants.name: First Nations Development Institute — Grantmaking Program
grants.geographicScope: National — grants made in 46 states plus DC as of year-end 2025
grants.type: National Native-led grantmaking and technical-assistance organization
grants.eligibilitySummary: Tribes, Native nonprofit organizations, and Native individuals; specific eligibility varies by open funding initiative.
grants.typicalAward: Varies by initiative — historically several thousand to low six figures per grant
grants.applicationStatus: Open — specific initiatives rotate; check current RFPs on their site
grants.howToApply: See firstnations.org/grantmaking/ for currently open funding initiatives and application portals
grants.deadlineNotes: Initiative-specific; no single fixed annual deadline
grants.pnwImpactFit: General national resource rather than PNW-specific — best cited as a track record / capacity-building partner rather than a guaranteed dollar source for a Seattle-specific narrative.

grants.name: Muckleshoot Charity Fund
grants.based: Auburn, WA (King County — Seattle metro area)
grants.geographicScope: Washington State, with priority to the local/regional area
focusAreas: programs serving communities of color and Native American programs
grants.eligibilitySummary: Organizations located in Washington State holding 501(c)(3) status, WA nonprofit status, government-agency status, or state-recognized public schools. No more than one grant per 12-month period.
grants.applicationStatus: Open — reviewed quarterly, no fixed annual deadline
grants.pnwImpactFit: Directly local to the Seattle metro area (King County) and funded by a sovereign Tribal nation — strong evidence of a genuine local Indigenous funding relationship for a Seattle-area impact narrative.
grants.sourceNotes: muckleshoot.nsn.us/charity-fund, Instrumentl grant listing, GrantedAI listing (cross-checked 2026-09-12)

grants.name: Tulalip Cares: Charitable Contributions Fund
grants.based: Tulalip, WA (Snohomish County — greater Seattle region)
grants.geographicScope: Washington State, with priority to Snohomish County / Marysville / Everett
grants.eligibilitySummary: U.S.-based 501(c)(3) charitable/educational organizations, or accredited K-12 institutions, operating within Washington State. Fund will not provide more than 50% of an organization's overall operating budget. One grant per 12-month period for successful applicants.
grants.typicalAward: Varies — over $50 million distributed to 245+ organizations since 1993
grants.howToApply: Complete the Charitable Fund Grant Application (PDF or Word) at tulalipcares.org and mail to the Tulalip Tribes Charitable Fund
grants.deadlineNotes: Quarterly deadlines; next listed deadline as of last check was March 1 — confirm current-cycle date on the site
grants.pnwImpactFit: Another directly local, Tribally-funded source in the greater Seattle region — pairs well with Muckleshoot Charity Fund to show multiple genuine local Tribal funding relationships.

grants.name: Satterberg Foundation — Reparative Action Fund / Core Support
grants.geographicScope: Washington State and California primarily; some funding in Arizona
grants.eligibilitySummary: No open, unsolicited application process. Core Support and the Reparative Action Fund operate by invitation/relationship only. Committed $50M over 10 years (from 2020) specifically to Black- and Indigenous-led organizations as part of a broader reparative strategy in WA, CA, and AZ.
grants.typicalAward: Multi-year, unrestricted; reported awards range roughly $500–$2.7M (median around $100K) across the foundation's full portfolio
grants.howToApply: No direct-apply pathway. Realistic path in is relationship-building (board/staff introductions, trusted intermediaries) rather than a cold application — do not budget this as a submit-and-wait funding source.
grants.pnwImpactFit: High-profile Seattle-based funder with an explicit Indigenous-led funding commitment, useful to name as an aspirational/relationship-building target — but should not be listed as a funding source you can apply to on a deadline.
grants.sourceNotes: satterberg.org/grantmaking/, Inside Philanthropy funder profile, Grantable/Instrumentl 990 summaries, hinchilla.com funder profile (cross-checked 2026-09-12)

grants.name: Administration for Native Americans (ANA) — FY2026 NOFOs
grants.funder: U.S. Dept. of Health & Human Services, Administration for Children and Families / ANA
grants.based: Federal (Washington, D.C.) — nationwide eligibility including PNW Tribes
grants.geographicScope: National — federally and non-federally recognized Tribes, Native Hawaiians, Alaska Natives
grants.eligibilitySummary: American Indian Tribes (federally- and non-federally-recognized), Native Hawaiian organizations, Alaska Native villages/organizations, Native American Pacific Islander organizations. Eligibility and match requirements are NOFO-specific.
grants.typicalAward: Varies sharply by NOFO — e.g. prior SEDS awards ran $100,000–$400,000 (20% match); FY2026 EAGLE/AI3 amounts are NOFO-specific
grants.applicationStatus: IMPORTANT — the long-running SEDS program was replaced for FY2026 by new NOFOs: EAGLE (Economic Advancement Grants for Local Empowerment, opportunity HHS-2026-ACF-ANA-NEG-0120) and the AI3 Action Institute (opportunity HHS-2026-ACF-ANA-NAI-0035); both had an application deadline of Aug 27, 2026, which has already passed as of this database's lastUpdated date. Separate FY2026 NOFOs for Environmental Regulatory Enhancement (ERE), Native Languages Preservation & Maintenance (P&M), and Esther Martinez Immersion (EMI) were also issued.
grants.howToApply: Monitor acf.gov/ana/grants and Grants.gov for the next open cycle of each program
grants.deadlineNotes: Check acf.gov/ana/grants for the next fiscal-year cycle — federal Native-American program structures have been actively changing (SEDS was discontinued/replaced in FY2026)
grants.pnwImpactFit: Not PNW-specific, but the Environmental Regulatory Enhancement (ERE) program is directly relevant to any Seattle-area Tribal applicant whose project touches environmental regulation/justice work adjacent to WA's HEAL Act.
grants.sourceNotes: acf.gov/ana and acf.gov/ana/grants, Tribal Business News (tribalbusinessnews.com) reporting on the SEDS-to-EAGLE/AI3 transition, federalgrantswire.com (cross-checked 2026-09-12) — this entry is the most time-sensitive in the database and should be re-verified before any application references it

grants.name: Protecting Native Places (PNP)
grants.funder: National Association of Tribal Historic Preservation Officers (NATHPO), with Mellon Foundation support
grants.geographicScope: National — open to Member Tribal Historic Preservation Officers (THPOs), which includes PNW Tribes with a THPO office
grants.eligibilitySummary: NATHPO Member Tribal Historic Preservation Officers (THPOs).
grants.applicationStatus: Cyclical — 2026 cycle was under review as of last check; monitor for next cycle
grants.deadlineNotes: Check nathpo.org for the next application window
grants.pnwImpactFit: Relevant specifically for PNW Tribes with an active THPO office doing cultural-site or historic-preservation work — a narrower fit than the general community/arts funders above but a strong match when applicable.
